messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

output:
Draft's at `/tmp/pr/pricing.md` (248 words, clean through the slopwatch gate). I used "Sift" as a placeholder name — swap it, and swap the numbers, which I invented.

---

# Pricing

Every plan reviews the whole diff, not a sample of it. Nothing is metered per suggestion.

## Solo — free

For one person, on public code. Sift reads every pull request you open, comments inline, and stays quiet about the formatting your linter already caught. Unlimited public repos, three private ones, 200 reviews a month. No card.

## Team — $19 per developer, per month

Where most people land. Private repos, no review cap, GitHub and GitLab. You write the house rules in a `sift.toml` file — no raw SQL outside `db/`, every new endpoint needs a rate limit — and Sift holds the line on them the way a picky senior would, with a file and a line number instead of a lecture. A 500-line diff comes back in about 90 seconds. Fourteen days free. Cancel from the dashboard; there is no call with anybody.

## Enterprise — talk to us

Runs in your VPC or on your own hardware, so nothing leaves your network. SAML SSO, audit logs, a SOC 2 Type II report on request, 99.9% uptime in writing. You also get a named engineer who has read your codebase and a shared Slack channel where they answer. Contracts start near $12k a year; the number moves with seat count and where you host it.

---

Move between plans whenever you want. We prorate, and seats you drop come back as credit — nobody gets billed for a developer who left in March.

---

Two things worth deciding before this ships: whether you want the Enterprise price visible at all (a range filters tire-kickers but invites anchoring), and whether the last line is a promise your billing system can actually keep.
